questions.q: Why did Caldwell Logistics choose Custom installation instead of Express when setting up Microsoft Entra Connect?
options: Express installation does not install on a member server
Custom installation is required for any company with more than 100 users
Express would sync every OU with password hash sync and no filtering, but Caldwell needed to scope sync to specific OUs
Express installation does not support password hash sync at all
questions.explain: Custom installation lets Caldwell select which OUs are in scope and pick password hash sync explicitly, rather than syncing everything by default.

questions.q: Why did Caldwell's team choose password hash sync over federation?
options: Password hash sync is required for companies with fewer than 1,000 users
Federation is no longer supported by Microsoft Entra Connect
Federation sends plain-text passwords to the cloud, which password hash sync avoids
It avoids standing up and maintaining an ADFS farm, keeping a smaller failure domain and native Conditional Access support
questions.explain: With a 2-person infrastructure team and no existing ADFS investment, PHS avoids a new on-prem single point of failure and lets Entra ID evaluate Conditional Access directly.

questions.q: What does the Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta cmdlet do?
options: Switches the sync method from password hash sync to federation
Permanently disables Microsoft Entra Connect
Forces an immediate incremental sync instead of waiting for the next scheduled cycle
Deletes all synced objects from Microsoft Entra ID
questions.explain: It triggers a delta sync on demand, which is useful for verifying a change synced without waiting on the default 30-minute schedule.

questions.q: In the Entra admin center, what indicates a user account is being synced from on-premises AD?
options: The user's profile shows "Directory synced: Yes" with a source of Windows Server AD
The user's license count shows as unlimited
The user is listed under the Conditional Access blade
The user has a green checkmark next to their display name
questions.explain: A synced user's profile explicitly shows the sync status and source, distinct from a cloud-only account.

questions.q: After confirming a user synced successfully, what else must be verified to know a Conditional Access policy actually applies to them?
options: Nothing further — a successful sync automatically applies every Conditional Access policy
Their sign-in logs show the policy as Success, and if the policy targets a synced group, that group's membership synced too
Conditional Access only applies to cloud-only accounts, never synced ones
The user must manually accept the policy via email
questions.explain: A policy scoped to a group only reaches users once that group's own membership has synced from on-prem AD; checking the sign-in log confirms the policy actually fired.
